gen-dafont-quantum-gf-noto-sans-ethiopic: Noto Sans Ethiopic reads sturdy and upright, its c terminals hanging well clear of the bowl so each line stays crisp. Quantum, in contrast, has no swelling in its bowls, and a long page of the body would feel steady.
gen-dafont-quantum-gf-noto-sans-glagolit: Round, open and quietly tough. gen-dafont-quantum-gf-noto-sans-grantha: Noto Sans Grantha reads smoothly, its letters like flattened pen-nib bowls. Over a long stretch it never snags on a closed-up bowl, while Quantum, traced as if with one marker, stays in the headline above.
gen-dafont-quantum-gf-noto-sans-gunjala-: Crayon-thick and cheerful. Noto Sans Gunjala Gondi cuts its terminals back to leave a big gap, and Quantum brings a marker-drawn plainness to every character, so the strongest quality here is how little either one fusses.
gen-dafont-quantum-gf-noto-sans-jp: Sleek, upright, and spaced out. Quantum holds its stroke thickness without variation, and Noto Sans JP sweeps its curves open with a very large x-height, so one does the shouting and the other does the talking.
gen-dafont-quantum-gf-noto-sans-khojki: Clean lines, wide exits, and a big clear eye on every e in the body. Noto Sans Khojki is a plain sans that lets light through, and Quantum strokes look drawn with a fixed pen, which is what ties them together.
gen-dafont-quantum-gf-noto-sans-khudawad: Approachable first, with Noto Sans Khudawadi keeping capitals and lowercase close in height and its rounds left unlatched like a hook. Quantum looks cut from strips of equal width, and it does its best work large and brief.
gen-dafont-quantum-gf-noto-sans-limbu: Gaping curves, big friendly letters. Quantum is stencil-cut at one steady width and gives a title real punch, while Noto Sans Limbu, a plain sans with tall-bodied small letters, is built to carry the words that follow.
gen-dafont-quantum-gf-noto-sans-lydian: Approachable and a bit cheeky, with Noto Sans Lydian keeping its capitals close to the lowercase and its openings as wide as a sprung paper clip. Quantum ends its terminals at the width they began, so the two sit together easily.
